events.text: It is the lamp, in the end. {npc} comes in with it while your back is turned, and the shadow on the paper door has tails in it, and {npc} screams, and the lamp goes down on the floor and the oil runs burning across the boards. Dogs, all down the street. Doors. Somebody shouting the word, the old word. The face you wore for years is gone in the time it takes to drop a lamp.
events.arc: The Shadow on the Paper Door

choices.text: Run, now, over the back wall and up the hill

ok.log: Over the wall, the barley, the dyke, the hill. The dogs lose you at the stream. From your mound you watch the lanterns going up and down the street all night, and hear your borrowed name shouted, and then the other name, the true one.

fail.log: The dogs catch you in the barley. You fight free with a torn flank and run the dyke on three legs, and lie in the earth for a month with the whole county hunting the hill above you. (-15 health)

choices.text: Stamp the fire out first, so the house does not burn, and then run

effects.log: You put out the oil with a quilt and your own feet, while {npc} watches from the yard, white. Then you go. Later {npc} tells the story with that in it, every time: it put the fire out first. Some people never believe that part. (-8 health)

choices.text: Turn at the door and look at {npc} once, before you go

mem.note: saw the fox under the face

effects.log: One look. Not a threat. {npc} stares back with the lamp-oil burning between you and something in the face changes, as if a question {npc} had for years had just been answered. Then you are gone.

events.text: The first face you ever lost. {npc} knew it best: years of market mornings, a hundred small kindnesses. And now {npc} is standing in the yard with the dogs, with the neighbours, with a stick in hand, looking at a fox with two tails backed against the wall of the house where you lived, and there is nothing in that face you recognise.
events.arc: The Shadow on the Paper Door

choices.text: Speak, in the old voice of the face: "It is still me"

ok.log: The voice they knew, from a fox's mouth. {npc} lowers the stick. The neighbours do not. In the moment of {npc}'s hesitation you are over the wall. Later you hear {npc} would not let them dig up the hill.

fail.log: The voice they knew, from a fox's mouth, is the most terrible thing {npc} has ever heard. The stick comes down. You are over the wall bleeding. (-12 health)

choices.text: Go, without a word. There is nothing a word could fix

effects.log: Over the wall without looking back. You will not go into that street again for a very long time, and when you do, nobody in it will remember, and the house will be gone, and you will still not look at it.

events.text: Years after the face fell, you go back to that town in another face, a stranger passing through, and stop at a wine-house, and hear it told. In their story you had nine tails, and ate children, and flew over the roofs on the night they found you. In their story the dogs saved everyone. The old people tell it to frighten the young, and the young laugh, and do not quite stop being frightened.
events.arc: The Shadow on the Paper Door

choices.text: Correct one detail, casually, as a stranger: "I heard it put the fire out first"

effects.log: An old person at the back of the room nods slowly. "That is right," they say. "I was there. It did." The room argues about it until closing time. In time, it is part of the story.

choices.text: Listen to the end, and pay, and go

effects.log: You are a monster in their story, and a stranger in their town. Both are safer than the truth. You go on up the road, lighter, and heavier, both.

events.text: In the morning the bead does not come back. {npc} swallowed it in the night, and ran out into the dark, and fell on the road, and lay looking at the ground as if it were a book. Half your light is in a human now. Something in your back folds, a tail you have carried a long time, flat against you like a wet feather, and the mountain feels very far away.

choices.text: Follow {npc}, unseen, wherever {he} goes

effects.log: You follow. {npc} walks differently now, looking down, stopping at crossroads to feel the ground through the soles of the feet. You stay a field away. You do not know yet how to ask for a thing a human swallowed.

choices.text: Let {him} have the night. Go home and bow to the moon with what is left

effects.log: The moon goes into half a bead. It is like drinking from a cracked bowl. Down in the village, a window is lit all night: {npc}, awake, writing something down very fast.

choices.text: Let {him} keep it. Begin a new bead from nothing, slowly

effects.log: You sit on the mound at moonrise and decide. The folded tail opens, slowly, empty. In your mouth there is a new grain of light, small as rice, the way it was at the beginning. Down in the village {npc} will become something. You will become something too, slower.

events.text: You know where your bead is the way you know where your own tail is: in the dark, without looking. It is in {npc}, in the next town, in a rented room above a dyer's shop. {npc} has stopped sleeping. People have started coming to the room with questions about wells and graves and where to dig, and {npc} answers every one of them right.

choices.text: Go in a face and ask for it, plainly

ok.log: A long night of talk, about wells and graves and what it is like to see the veins of the earth. At dawn {npc} gives it back on a breath, freely, and is suddenly very tired and very ordinary and very relieved. "It was too much," {npc} says. The folded tail opens.

fail.log: {npc} looks at you, and sees the earth under your face, and the fox under that. "No," {npc} says, very afraid, and shuts the door. You will have to come back. (-5 health)

choices.text: Frighten it out of {him}: foxfire in the room, a voice in the dark

effects.log: It comes up out of {npc} in a scream, and you catch it in your mouth and are gone. The tail opens. Behind you {npc} sits shaking in the dark and will never answer a question about wells again, or sleep without a lamp.

choices.text: Leave it with {him}. The town needs those answers more than you need a tail

effects.log: You go home and begin again with a grain of light. In the next town {npc} becomes the geomancer three counties send for, and never once chooses a bad site, and never knows why the fox on the hill road always looks so pleased.

events.text: The one who kept your bead is old now and famous, and three provinces send for the geomancer who never chooses a bad site. Today the geomancer's procession passes below your hill, and stops, and the old geomancer gets down and climbs, slowly, with a stick, to your mound, and sits on it, and says to the grass: "I know you are there. I only wanted to say: it was the best life. Thank you."

choices.text: Come out and sit beside the old geomancer for a while

effects.log: You sit side by side looking at the valley, a fox and an old human, and the geomancer tells you where every vein of qi in it runs. You know them all already. You let the geomancer tell you anyway.

choices.text: Stay in the grass, and let the thanks be enough

effects.log: The geomancer waits a while, smiles, and goes down to the procession. On the mound, afterwards, there is a small dish of rice cakes, set exactly where the earth's qi comes up strongest.

events.text: A salt peddler on the hill road at dusk, pole on the shoulders, stick in hand, coming your way. Every fox learns the rule in the earth before it learns to hunt: never cross a salt peddler. The salt, the stick, the slow eyes. You are in the middle of the road in a borrowed face, and it is too late to be anywhere else.

choices.text: Step off the road into the grass and let the peddler pass, head down

effects.log: The peddler passes. The stick taps the stones, once, near your feet, and the pole creaks, and the slow voice says "good evening" without turning. You stand in the grass until the tapping is gone.

choices.text: Walk on and pass on the road, at arm's length, as people do

ok.log: You pass. Neither of you looks. Ten paces on, you hear the peddler stop, and turn, and stand looking at your back. You do not run. It is the hardest thing you do all year.

fail.log: The stick comes out sideways across the road, quick as a snake, and taps your shin, and your face slips like oil on water. You are in the grass before the second tap. Behind you, the slow laugh. (-5 health)

events.text: A dog at the door again: a new one, a stray this time, sitting in the road outside your house with its head on one side, barking once every few breaths, the way dogs do when they have something to say and are going to keep saying it. The street is getting used to it. The street is starting to wonder what the dog is trying to say.

choices.text: Feed it, every night, until it decides you are its

effects.log: It takes a month. Then it lies on your step instead of in the road, and growls at everybody else who comes near, which the street finds very funny, and much less interesting.

choices.text: Lead it away by night, three valleys off, with a trail of scent

effects.log: Three valleys. It follows the scent all night, happily, and wakes up somewhere else, and stays. Dogs are like that. You walk home at dawn wishing people were.

choices.text: Hide the tails, and go out the back way for a season

effects.log: A season of the back gate. The dog sits at the front, barking at a door nobody uses, and in the end the street decides it is mad, and somebody takes it in.

events.text: The full moon, and you are in company: a feast, a funeral, a long night of talk with the neighbours on the veranda. Under a full moon the face goes thin as paper, and the tails press against it like a hand against a screen. Everyone is in the moonlight. Everyone can see everyone.

choices.text: Sit in the shadow of the eaves all night, out of the moon

effects.log: You stay under the eaves. Somebody calls you shy. Somebody else calls you rude. Nobody calls you anything else, which was the point.

choices.text: Leave early, with an excuse

effects.log: A sick relative, a hearth to bank, a headache. You go home and sit in the earth under the mound and bow to the same moon with your tails out, alone, and hear them laughing on the veranda two fields away.

choices.text: Stay in the moonlight with them, and trust the face

ok.log: It holds. All night, in the full moon, among them. The bead drinks the light and the face drinks the company and in the morning you are tired and happy in a way you did not know you were made for.

fail.log: Somebody's child, sleepy against your arm, says in a small voice, "Your shadow has a tail." The adults laugh. The child does not.

events.text: A knock at dusk. A mother, an old father, a younger brother, it is a different one each time: the family of one of the pale ones, come to the neighbour who knows herbs, or knows the hills, or just seems to know things, to ask if there is anything at all for a wasting that will not stop. They do not know who they are asking.

choices.text: Go with them, and give the breath back with the bead

ok.log: In the dark room the bead passes on your breath and comes back. In the morning the pale one sits up and asks for rice. The family weeps on your step. One breath given back. (Breath debt -1)

fail.log: The bead passes on your breath and the pale one swallows it, half asleep. The colour comes back, and something else: a look at the floor as if it were a map. The bead does not come back. A tail folds.

choices.text: Give them herbs, honestly, and say there is nothing else

effects.log: Angelica, jujube, a little ginseng. They thank you for it with the terrible gratitude of people who know it will not be enough. You close the door. The debt stays where it is.
